correctness.rationale: Tirfe et al. model (2.1) prints V'=alpha*Pi-(eta+mu)V and I'=beta*I*S/N+(1-p)*eta*V-hI, h=omega+mu+xi>0. Under alpha,Pi,eta,mu>0,0<p<1 and nonnegative states with N>0, V(t)->alpha*Pi/(eta+mu). Because incidence is nonnegative, variation of constants gives liminf I>= (1-p)*eta*alpha*Pi/((eta+mu)*h)>0. At any equilibrium, I*>=that same positive number, so proposed disease-free I*=0 with V*>0 is not an equilibrium. Independent exact witness Pi=2,alpha=1/2,eta=mu=omega=1,p=1/2,xi=0 gives residual 1/4 and floor 1/8.

originality.rationale: The exact published SVITR model includes a density-independent vaccinated-to-infected inflow, while the paper nonetheless evaluates threshold and bifurcation criteria at a proposed I=0 equilibrium. General next-generation theory already requires an invariant disease-free set; the source-specific contradiction and quantified asymptotic infective floor are the assessed correction, not a newly claimed general threshold method.
residual_risks: This assesses model (2.1) as printed; a corrected model with infection-dependent vaccinated flow could remove the obstruction.
No assertion that a positive equilibrium exists uniquely or is stable, nor about controlled equations.
The disease-free method failure is a standard principle; originality is the source-specific exposed inconsistency and strict quantitative floor.

value.rationale: The obstruction invalidates a named disease-free fixed point and every local stability/bifurcation interpretation based on it for the actually printed nondegenerate vector field. The explicit positive liminf lower bound quantifies how long-time infection cannot vanish even when transmission is negligible. This addresses a central structural error, not a minor algebraic typo.

limitations: Requires Pi,alpha,eta,mu>0; 0<p<1, N>0 and nonnegative state trajectory.
No conclusion for degenerate cases p=1, alpha=0, Pi=0, or eta=0.
